title: One-Sided Differentiability of Piecewise Join
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Determine whether f(x) = x^2 for x <= 0 and f(x) = x for x > 0 is differentiable at x = 0.
finalAnswer: f \text{ is continuous at } x = 0, \text{ but not differentiable because } f'_-(0) = 0 \neq 1 = f'_+(0)

steps.title: Compute Left-Hand Derivative at 0
steps.explanation: Use the left parabola branch x^2 for h < 0.
steps.why: Left-hand derivative uses values strictly less than 0.

steps.title: Compute Right-Hand Derivative at 0
steps.explanation: Use the right linear branch x for h > 0.
steps.why: Right-hand derivative uses values strictly greater than 0.

steps.title: Conclude
steps.mathExpression: f'_-(0) = 0 \neq 1 = f'_+(0) \implies f'(0) \text{ does not exist}
steps.explanation: The tangent slope jumps abruptly from 0 to 1 at x = 0.
steps.why: Differentiability requires left and right derivatives to match.
